state.repo: dhanesh/agent-skills: a collection of agent skills that together form a software factory (idea, spec, design, build, verify, review, release, operate, support, growth, knowledge, governance). A pipeline skill can move work between stages on a timer; a human holds every merge, deploy, spend, external message and delete.
state.rubric:
Status rubric. A row's status judges the stage's core job only. How work passes from one stage to the next is judged in the Stage handoffs row.

- `covered`: one or more skills do the stage's core job, and no limit weakens it.
- `covered, with limits`: the skills do the core job. The row names each limit that weakens the proof or leaves a step to you. A limit that you chose (launch, pricing, spend, merge, deploy, external messages) does not lower a row.
- `partly`: part of the core job has no skill. The row names that part after "Limits:".
- `missing`: no skill does the core job.
- `out of scope, by design`: the owner decided that the factory does not do this stage.

Limit tags. The text after "Limits:" is a list of items separated by `;`. Each item starts with exactly one tag: `[decision]` (a limit that you chose), `[trust]` (a limit on how far the proof can be trusted, for example a claim that no tool checks) or `[open]` (a gap that the factory still has). A row whose items are all `[decision]` is `covered`.

s_idea_validation.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Idea validation' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `idea-validation` turns an idea into a brief whose riskiest assumptions each carry a test, a metric, pass and kill thresholds and a deadline, registers it before any result, computes GO, KILL, STALLED or PENDING from the results you report, flags a critical assumption you drop later, and hands a `go` to `spec-first-planning` as an `idea-brief/v1` envelope; `factory-pipeline` lists each idea with an assumption due within 3 days or expired, and plans each `go` idea once. Limits: [decision] you run every experiment (the agent never publishes, sends or spends); [decision] you record each experiment result and make each decision, so the stage cannot run unattended; [trust] results are claimed, not proven

s_test_verify.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Test / verify' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `verifier-installer`, `test-safety-net`; `verification-skill-forge` generates a verify skill that drives the running app and records SHA-bound evidence, which `factory-conductor`'s evidence gate requires before a merge. A feature can also state a contract whose clauses carry a stronger proof: `proved` (Verus), `bounded` (Kani) or `property` (proptest, Hypothesis, fast-check, rapid), with a caught mutant for the last two. A plan's `[tier: ...]` hint sets the weakest tier the gate accepts, and `verifier-installer` prints one `BACKEND:` line for each of these proof tools it finds. Limits: [trust] no `proved` or `bounded` backend for Python, TypeScript or Go yet

s_operate_planning.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Operate → planning' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `ops-intake` reads failed releases, failing CI on the default branch, GitHub issues and (through a JSON-lines transform) Jira or Linear, ranks them into a local queue, and hands each picked item to `spec-first-planning` as an `intake-item/v1` envelope; a verified release that holds the fix marks it resolved. `intake sweep` runs the read-only sources you committed, and `intake autopick` picks items that match the pick policy you registered; `factory-pipeline` runs both on a schedule. Limits: [trust] it cannot enforce that MCP calls are read-only; [open] a squash merge resolves its item only when the run-result names the PR, and `factory-conductor` does not write the PR number yet; [decision] rebase merges and partial runs need your `resolve`; [decision] items outside your pick policy wait for you; [decision] Jira and Linear come in through documented conversion recipes, not dedicated readers

s_governance.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Governance' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `security-posture-audit`, `base-in-reality`, `agent-ready-rails` (audit), `crafting-self-prompting-loops` (per-loop budget), `factory-conductor` (run token and dollar caps, enforced when the grant opts in, metered from the usage the agent claims from its harness; a project money ledger whose check only refuses a spend over the human's monthly caps and never approves one, so every spend stays the human's decision and recorded spend is a claim). The autonomy grant is the gate policy of skill-contract commandment 10, and six skills check it before they act. A pipeline grant (7 days at most) caps plans per day, open runs and dispatches per day, every grant derived from it names it, and the kill switch revokes them all. Limits: [trust] token and dollar caps are metered from usage that the agent claims; [trust] the pipeline's own state folder, which holds the cap counts, is outside the tamper check
